chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: Seeking one’s best judgment is always sufficient when it is not known where the direction of the qiblah is.

key_terms.أَبَدًا: at all times or always in such cases
key_terms.التَّحَرِّي: exerting effort to determine the most likely correct direction
key_terms.لَمْ يُعْلَمْ: when it is not known with certainty
key_terms.وَجْهُ الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of the qiblah toward which salat is performed
key_terms.يَجْزِي: is sufficient or valid in fulfilling the requirement

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they do not know the direction of the qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning uncertainty about the qiblah. It states that when the direction of the qiblah is unknown, acting on one’s best determination is sufficient.
